themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Applied Digital's CEO and President bought about $6.66 million of stock on Oct 16 at $18.04 to $18.86 (filed Oct 19), after a 22% drop in a week; it is the first insider buying there since May 2023, and its main tenant is CoreWeave. On Oct 19 Goldman upgraded CoreWeave to Buy, calling debt fears overblown, and ARK bought about 132,500 CRWV shares, yet CRWV still closed down 0.44% at $61.12. The rebound faded overnight when Seoul AI data center firm Elice fell about 30% on its Kosdaq debut.
themes.for_you: No action. APLD has no dashboard verdict yet and is falling, so the insider buy is a watch item, not a buy. CRWV is left out of both lists: an upgrade and ARK buying pull one way, 15% bond yields the other. No puts on CRWV or ORCL.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: Korea's LS Electric booked a $138.5 million order from Bloom Energy for 38 kV switchgear and transformers for Bloom fuel cells at a Pennsylvania data center, delivering April to July 2027 (DCD, Oct 2026). DCD says the site is likely Aligned's Project Phoenix campus at Shippingport, where Bloom may deploy up to 2 GW. The same week nuclear names kept falling: Barclays cut NuScale to Underweight and it hit a new 52 week low (24/7 Wall St, Oct 20), with Oklo down about 5%.
themes.for_you: BE (221.31 on Oct 16) stays 'Buy zone, wait for the chart': sellers still lead (up/down 0.85), and it reports around Oct 27, so no put yet. Fuel cells ship now; small reactors are years away and need cheap money, which 5% plus Treasury yields deny. No action on SMR or OKLO.

themes.name: Defense, drones and reshoring
themes.what: RTX reported Q3 sales of $25.0 billion, up 11%, and adjusted EPS of $2.26 against about $1.78 expected; backlog reached $340 billion, $164 billion of it defense, helped by multiyear Tomahawk and AMRAAM missile contracts. It raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guide to $7.65 to $7.75 (company release, Oct 20).
themes.for_you: RTX (193.92 on Oct 16) is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' because sellers led on volume (up/down 0.74). The report is out of the way now. Wait for up/down volume back above 1.0 and a 'Buy zone now' verdict before any long term buy or put.

innovations.name: Energy
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Behind the meter power keeps adding real orders: LS Electric booked $138.5 million of switchgear for Bloom fuel cells at a Pennsylvania data center, likely Aligned's Project Phoenix where Bloom may supply up to 2 GW (DCD). Fervo's Cape Station is running and it is hosting an investor open house, while JPMorgan cut its target to $27 on Oct 19. Small reactor stocks hit new lows on a Barclays downgrade of NuScale (Oct 20). No stage moves.
innovations.for_you: No action. BE (221.31) is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' and reports around Oct 27, so no put before then. Skip SMR and OKLO: high rates hurt projects that need years of cheap funding.

countries.name: China
countries.what: On Oct 16 China made companies register before exporting a list of AI, biotech and solar technologies, effective at once, and proposed banning exports of 12 solar manufacturing methods, including advanced wafer, perovskite and tandem cell know how (pv magazine, Geopolitechs). Finished panels are not covered. Public comment runs to Nov 15.
countries.for_you: No action. FSLR is left out of both lists: keeping know how in China protects Chinese makers' lead, but it also slows foreign rivals building plants abroad. Watch the Nov 15 comment deadline as a sign of how hard Beijing plays before the Jan 10 rare earth date.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: The Russia waiver dip did not hold: Brent fell to $106.82 on Oct 19 but settled at $109.55, and traded above $110 early Oct 20 after Houthi claims of strikes on Yanbu and Shaybah (unconfirmed). Energy Secretary Wright said Gulf flows are back to about 80% of prewar levels and the US will let some sanctioned dark fleet tankers carry legal crude; Kpler estimates only about 24 ships qualify.
countries.for_you: If you hold energy swings, keep the dashboard stops; oil held up. Treat the 80% figure as a government claim until shipping data confirm it. LNG and FRO are left out of both lists: more legal tankers could ease freight rates, but Kpler expects little effect.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: Seoul sold the AI rebound on Oct 20: the KOSPI was down 2.8% at 5,607.95 early (AFP) and about 3.65% later in the session, below 5,600, with SK hynix and Samsung leading. Elice, an AI data center firm, fell about 30% on its Kosdaq debut despite retail demand over 400 times the shares offered (Seoul Economic Daily, TechNode). Closing levels were not confirmed at writing.
countries.for_you: No action. Korean bank ADRs KB (118.81) and SHG (70.31, Oct 16 closes) stay hurt into Thursday's Bank of Korea decision. A failed AI listing is one more sign lenders and buyers are pulling back from data center bets.
